header.userPrompt:
Fix how the bank-statement review flow handles import rules and credit (positive-amount) rows. These are four tightly related changes to the same flow; implement them together.

## Context
Import rules match a row's description via `ImportRuleMatcher` (normalized substring contains). `RowRuleVerdict.verdict` turns a match into Ignore / SetMerchant / SetCategory / NoRule. `BankStatementReviewLogic.resolveImport` + `rowInfo` decide what importing a row would create and whether a row `isReady`. Today the whole ready/auto-import pipeline is debit-only (`row.amount < 0`), and a `set_merchant` rule whose merchant has no default category silently resolves to nothing (the row shows no merchant and is not ready). Refund fields (`CreateRefund.Request`: merchantId, categoryId, expenseId) are all optional.

## 1. Require a fully-allocated category on every expense
In `ExpenseValidator.validate` (server/.../actions/expenses/ExpenseValidator.scala): the splits must cover the full expense amount. Replace the current `splits.map(_._2).sum > amount` rejection with a rejection when `splits.map(_._2).sum != amount` (the sum must equal `amount`). This also forces at least one split, since an empty split list sums to 0 which never equals a positive amount. Keep the existing duplicate-category and non-positive-split-amount checks. This validator is already shared by CreateExpenseAction, UpdateExpenseAction and CreateExpenseFromRowAction, so all three are covered.
Frontend: the expense create and edit forms must block submission when the splits do not cover the full amount (no category, or a remainder left unallocated) and surface the validation message.

## 2. A set_merchant rule prefills the merchant even without a category (debit rows)
In `BankStatementReviewLogic`: a `SetMerchant` verdict whose merchant has no default category currently makes `resolveImport` return `None`, so nothing shows. Keep `resolveImport` returning `None` in that case (the row is not one-click ready, because an expense now requires a category), but add a `prefillMerchantId: Option[UUID]` to `RowInfo`, populated from the verdict's merchant regardless of whether a category resolved. Such a debit row stays out of the Ready tab and shows under Unprocessed, but now displays the merchant.
`BankRowCreateExpenseForm` must initialise its merchant field from `prefillMerchantId` so that opening the row lands on a form with the merchant already filled and only the category left to pick.

## 3. Ignore rules apply to credits too
In `BankStatementReviewLogic.rowInfo`, the `isReady` computation gates on `row.amount < 0`. An `Ignore` verdict must make a row ready regardless of sign, so ignore rules work on positive (credit) rows as well as debits. (This is what makes ignore rules like `TRASPASO ALEXIS` take effect on the credit rows they match.)

## 4. Rule-matched credits resolve to refunds, shown in Ready and processed in bulk
A positive-amount row that a `SetMerchant` or `SetCategory` rule matches must resolve to a prefilled refund and appear in the Ready tab. Because a refund's merchant, category and expense link are all optional, even a category-less merchant rule fully resolves a refund.
- Add a refund resolver in `BankStatementReviewLogic`, e.g. `resolveRefund(verdict, merchants, row): Option[RefundPrefill]`, carrying optional merchantId and optional categoryId from the winning rule.
- `isReady` must let a credit row through when it resolves to a refund (or has an Ignore verdict, per change 3). `primaryActionFor` already routes `isReady && row.amount > 0` to `ReviewRefund`; keep that.
- `BankRowCreateRefundForm` must prefill its merchant/category from the resolved refund.
- `Process ready` (bulk): add a `BulkRowDecision.CreateRefund(prefill)` case and handle it in the bulk runner so the one-click bulk action creates these refunds (and ignores the ignore-matched credit rows). Credits whose rule is Ignore are ignored in bulk; credits whose rule sets a merchant/category have a refund created.
- Refund-to-expense linking is out of scope: create the refunds unlinked (`expenseId = None`).

## Tests
- `ExpenseValidatorSpec`: splits summing to less than the amount fail (including empty splits); splits summing exactly to the amount pass.
- `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`: (a) an Ignore verdict on a credit row is ready; (b) a SetMerchant-with-no-category debit row is not ready but exposes `prefillMerchantId`; (c) a SetMerchant credit row resolves to a refund and is ready; (d) `bulkRowDecision` returns `CreateRefund` for a rule-matched credit and `Ignore` for an ignore-matched credit.
- Frontend form specs: expense form blocks submit when the amount is not fully split; the create-expense form prefills the merchant from a matched set_merchant rule; the refund form prefills from a matched rule.

Do not add refund-to-expense auto-linking, and do not add a required default category to the merchant model. Keep existing reviewer and commit-message conventions.

resultJson.description:
Make the bank-statement review flow treat import rules consistently across debit and credit rows, and make every expense fully categorised. Today the ready/auto-import pipeline in `BankStatementReviewLogic` is debit-only (`row.amount < 0`), so ignore rules and merchant/category rules do nothing on positive (credit) rows. A `set_merchant` rule whose merchant has no default category also resolves to nothing, so the row shows no merchant even though the rule matched. Meanwhile the backend accepts expenses with no splits or with splits that only partly cover the amount.

After this epic: (1) `ExpenseValidator` rejects any expense whose split amounts do not sum exactly to the expense amount, which also makes an empty split list invalid. The expense create and edit forms on ExpensesPage block submit and show the message. (2) A debit row matched by a category-less `set_merchant` rule stays out of Ready (an expense needs a category), but `RowInfo.prefillMerchantId` exposes the merchant. The table shows it, and the create-expense drawer opens with the merchant filled in. (3) An Ignore verdict makes a row ready whatever its sign. (4) A credit row matched by a SetMerchant/SetCategory rule resolves to a `RefundPrefill` (optional merchant, optional category). It is ready, opens a prefilled refund form, and "Process ready" creates it as an unlinked refund (`expenseId = None`) through a new `BulkRowDecision.CreateRefund`. Ignore-matched credits are ignored in bulk.

Out of scope: refund-to-expense auto-linking, and a required default category on merchants. Known side effect to call out in the PR: `ConfirmReceiptAction` (receipt confirmation) also uses `ExpenseValidator`, so confirming a receipt with partial or empty splits will now fail too. The task text only names Create/Update/CreateFromRow. ReceiptsPage frontend validation is not part of this epic, but the server specs it breaks must be updated.

tasks.title: Require splits to fully cover the expense amount (backend)
tasks.description: In server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/ExpenseValidator.scala replace `splits.map(_._2).sum > amount` with `!= amount`. Pick a clear message, e.g. "Split amounts must add up to the expense amount". Keep the amount>0, notes-length, duplicate-category and non-positive-split checks in their current order. Add server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/ExpenseValidatorSpec.scala (`validate` should …): empty splits fail; splits summing to less than the amount fail; splits summing to more fail; splits summing exactly to the amount pass (needs a real user + category via RepositoryUtils / withRepositories so the category lookup succeeds). Then fix existing server specs that relied on empty or partial splits. Known ones: controllers/ExpensesControllerSpec (`createRequest` defaults `splits = Nil`, plus the 'no splits', 'less than total' and 'clear splits on update with empty list' cases; turn the latter into failure assertions via `.expectError` or give them full splits), controllers/DocumentsControllerSpec ('create expense with partial splits (sum < amount)' via ConfirmReceiptAction), and any BankStatementsControllerSpec / McpControllerSpec cases that create expenses through these actions with no or partial splits. Grep the server tests for createExpense/createExpenseFromRow/confirm calls. Verify: `sbt "server/testOnly *ExpenseValidatorSpec *ExpensesControllerSpec *DocumentsControllerSpec *BankStatementsControllerSpec"` (Docker needed), plus `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Block expense create/edit submit when splits don't cover the amount (frontend)
tasks.description: In web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/ExpensesPage.scala, handleCreate and handleUpdate must refuse to call the API and `setError(...)` when the splits that will be sent do not sum exactly to the amount. That covers no category at all and an unallocated remainder. Extract a pure function on the ExpensesPage/ExpenseList object, e.g. `splitsError(amount: BigDecimal, splits: List[BigDecimal]): Option[String]`, using the same message as the backend. Apply it to the splits actually sent: for create that is `explicit` or else `merchantDefaultSplits(...)` (a merchant default category counts as a full single split); for edit it is `toUpdateSplits(editSplits)`. Don't change the existing 'Uncategorized: $rem' remainder display. Add cases to web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/ExpensesPageSpec.scala: no splits → error; partial → error; over-allocated → error; exact (single and multiple splits) → None. Verify with `sbt "web/testOnly *ExpensesPageSpec"` (Node 24 must be on PATH).

tasks.title: Prefill merchant for category-less set_merchant debits; Ignore rules apply to credits
tasks.description: In web/.../BankStatementReviewLogic.scala add `prefillMerchantId: Option[UUID]` to `RowInfo` and set it in `rowInfo` from `RowRuleVerdict.merchantId(verdict)`, whether or not a category resolved. `resolveImport` stays unchanged and still returns None when the merchant has no default category. Change `isReady` so an Ignore verdict makes an open row ready regardless of sign: `open && (verdict == Ignore || (row.amount < 0 && resolved.isDefined))`. Make `RowInfo.merchantName` fall back to the prefill merchant's name when `resolved` gives no merchant, so the Unprocessed row shows it (BankStatementReviewRow.matchCell reads `info.merchantName`). Update every `RowInfo(...)` construction in tests (BankStatementReviewRowSpec builds them positionally). BankRowCreateExpenseForm: `initialSelection` already returns (rule merchant, its categoryId = None) for a category-less SetMerchant winner, from the same verdict that `prefillMerchantId` uses. Confirm that path and add a BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec case, "prefill the merchant with no category for a SetMerchant rule whose merchant has no default category". Only add plumbing if the existing path doesn't hold, and avoid duplicate derivations. BankStatementReviewLogicSpec: Ignore on a credit row → isReady (and primaryActionFor gives IgnoreByRule); category-less SetMerchant debit → !isReady, resolved None, prefillMerchantId = Some(mid), merchantName = Some(name); bulkRowDecision on an ignore-matched credit → Ignore. Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec *BankStatementReviewRowSpec *BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec"`.

tasks.title: Resolve rule-matched credits to refunds and create them in bulk
tasks.description: In BankStatementReviewLogic add `final case class RefundPrefill(merchantId: Option[UUID], categoryId: Option[UUID])` and `resolveRefund(verdict, merchants, row): Option[RefundPrefill]`. It returns None unless `row.amount > 0`. SetMerchant(mid) → RefundPrefill(Some(mid), that merchant's default categoryId, if any). SetCategory(cid) → RefundPrefill(None, Some(cid)). Ignore/NoRule → None. Do not consult AI. Add `refund: Option[RefundPrefill]` to RowInfo. Recommended: compute `resolved` only for debits so a credit can never become a `Create` (expense) decision. isReady becomes `open && (verdict == Ignore || (amount<0 && resolved.isDefined) || (amount>0 && refund.isDefined))`, and primaryActionFor already routes ready credits to ReviewRefund. Make `merchantName`/`categoryName` cover the refund's ids, and make BankStatementReviewRow.categoryCell show the refund category: it currently matches only on `info.resolved`. Add `BulkRowDecision.CreateRefund(prefill: RefundPrefill)`. In `bulkRowDecision`, Ignore still wins, then `info.flatMap(_.refund)` → CreateRefund, then the existing expense-match logic. In BankStatementBulkRuns.handleBulkImport handle CreateRefund: call `client.createRefundFromRow(stmtId, rowId, CreateRefundFromRow.Request(amount = row.amount.abs, date = row.date, merchantId = p.merchantId, categoryId = p.categoryId, expenseId = None, notes = Some(row.description).filter(_.nonEmpty)))`; on success set `refundId = Some(resp.refundId)` on the row and count it under `created`; on failure call fail(ex.getMessage). The match must stay exhaustive (-Werror). Tests in BankStatementReviewLogicSpec: a SetMerchant credit (merchant with and without a default category) and a SetCategory credit resolve to a refund and are ready; a credit with no rule is not ready; bulkRowDecision → CreateRefund for a rule-matched credit. Check BankStatementBulkRunsSpec and update or extend it if it enumerates decisions. Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec *BankStatementReviewRowSpec *BankStatementBulkRunsSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Prefill the refund form from the matched rule
tasks.description: BankRowCreateRefundForm currently prefills only from a SetMerchant winner (merchant plus its default category) and ignores SetCategory rules. Extract a pure `initialSelection(row, ruleList, merchants, categories): (Option[GetMerchants.Response.Merchant], Option[UUID])` on the BankRowCreateRefundForm object. Build it on `BankStatementReviewLogic.resolveRefund(RowRuleVerdict.verdict(ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(ruleList, merchants.map(m => m.id -> m.name)), row.description), merchants, row)` and drop ids missing from the loaded merchants/categories, as BankRowCreateExpenseForm.initialSelection does. Use it to seed merchantInput/merchantIdOpt/categoryInput/categoryIdOpt. Add web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/BankRowCreateRefundFormSpec.scala (pure AnyWordSpec, no DOM): a SetMerchant rule prefills merchant and its default category; a category-less SetMerchant prefills only the merchant; a SetCategory rule prefills only the category; a merchant-name match (no explicit rule) prefills the merchant; an Ignore rule or no match gives (None, None); an unknown category id is dropped. Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *BankRowCreateRefundFormSpec"`.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules
- `lib/api/shared/` — shared Tapir endpoints and models. `net.wiringbits.api.utils.ImportRuleMatcher` (Rule(id, action, pattern), `effectiveRules(explicit, merchants: List[(UUID,String)])` adds an implicit SetMerchant rule per merchant name, `findRowWinner`, `normalize`). `RowRuleVerdict` (sealed `Verdict`: NoRule | Ignore | SetMerchant(merchantId) | SetCategory(categoryId); `verdict(rules, description)`, `merchantId(v)`, `categoryId(v)`). Models: `bankstatements.CreateRefundFromRow.Request(amount, date, merchantId: Option, categoryId: Option, expenseId: Option, notes: Option)` → `Response(refundId)`; `CreateExpenseFromRow.Request(amount, date, time, merchantId, notes, splits: List[Split(categoryId, amount)], receiptId)`. `ApiClient.createRefundFromRow(stmtId, rowId, req)`, `createExpenseFromRow`, `ignoreRow`.
- `server/` — Play backend. `server/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/ExpenseValidator.scala`: `validate(userId, amount, notes, merchantId, splits: List[(UUID, BigDecimal)]): Future[Unit]`. It fails with `Future.failed(new RuntimeException(msg))`, and the message reaches clients as the error string (`.expectError` in controller specs). Used by CreateExpenseAction, UpdateExpenseAction, bankstatements/CreateExpenseFromRowAction **and receipts/ConfirmReceiptAction**.
- `web/` — Scala.js + Slinky + MUI. Bank review code lives in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`:
  - `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala`: pure logic, no React. Holds `ResolvedImport(merchantId: Option[UUID], categoryId: UUID, categoryFromAi)`, `resolveImport(verdict, merchants, aiSuggestions, row)`, `RowInfo(verdict, resolved, isReady, merchantName, categoryName, linkedMerchantName, linkedCategory)`, `rowInfo(ruleList /*already effective rules*/, merchants, categories, ai, row)`, `primaryActionFor(row, isReady, verdict)`, enum `BulkRowDecision {Ignore; Link(expenseId); Create(resolved); Fail(msg)}`, `bulkRowDecision(info, expenseMatch, linkedThisRun)`, `expenseMatches` (debit-only, keep that), `bulkImportSummary(linked, created, ignored, failed)`, and `filterRows` ("ready" tab = isReady; default tab = open rows). The open-row condition is `row.expenseId.isEmpty && row.refundId.isEmpty && row.ignoredAt.isEmpty`.
  - `BankStatementBulkRuns.scala`: `handleBulkImport` loops sequentially over the selected ids, matches on `bulkRowDecision`, calls the API and updates rows via `setStatementRows(cur => cur.map(...copy(...)))`, with `succeed(counts.copy(...))`/`fail(msg)` helpers.
  - `BankStatementReviewContent.scala` builds `rowInfoById` and passes the selected ids to handleBulkImport. `BankStatementReviewRow.scala` `matchCell` reads `info.merchantName`. `categoryCell` matches on `info.resolved` (shows `info.categoryName` + an "AI" tag), so a refund needs its own branch. `BankStatementReviewDrawer.scala` renders the forms with (row, merchants, categories, ruleList = explicit rules, aiSuggestion).
  - `BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala`: pure helpers on the object (`initialSelection`, `rowVerdict` which applies `effectiveRules` itself, `initialMerchantInput`, `isPristine`, `ruleHint`, …), then the component. A SetMerchant winner already yields `(Some(merchant), merchant.categoryId)`.
  - `BankRowCreateRefundForm.scala`: no pure helpers yet. It inlines the SetMerchant-only prefill at the top of the component; fields are merchantInput/merchantIdOpt/categoryInput/categoryIdOpt.
  - `ExpensesPage.scala` (object `ExpenseList`, component around line 152): `parseSplits`, `toUpdateSplits`, `merchantDefaultSplits(merchantIdStr, amount)`, `handleCreate` (sends explicit splits, else the merchant default), `handleUpdate`, `splitRemainder`, `splitsSection`. Errors are shown via `setError(...)`.

## Tests and conventions
- docs/guide/testing.md: `"method" should { "behaviour" in {...} }`. Never put the class name in `should`. Spec paths mirror source paths. Frontend: test pure functions with plain AnyWordSpec and avoid DOM tests (RULE-TE-010). Backend DB tests use `withRepositories()` + `RepositoryUtils` factories (createUser, category creation; no raw SQL) and `.futureValue`; `intercept[RuntimeException](f.futureValue)` or `.expectError` for failures. No action specs exist by policy, but the task explicitly asks for `ExpenseValidatorSpec` (a validator, which is allowed). Put it at server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/expenses/ExpenseValidatorSpec.scala and construct it as `new ExpenseValidator(repositories.merchants, repositories.categories)` with an implicit ec. Check the repository field names in RepositoryUtils/RepositorySpec.
- Existing specs to extend: web/src/test/.../BankStatementReviewLogicSpec.scala, BankStatementReviewRowSpec.scala (builds `RowInfo` positionally at ~line 51/61, so adding fields breaks compilation there), BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec.scala, BankStatementBulkRunsSpec.scala, ExpensesPageSpec.scala.
- Server specs that rely on empty or partial splits and will break: controllers/ExpensesControllerSpec (`createRequest(..., splits = Nil)` default, 'no splits', 'less than total', 'clear splits on update with empty list'), controllers/DocumentsControllerSpec ('partial splits (sum < amount)' via receipt confirm). Grep BankStatementsControllerSpec/McpControllerSpec for createExpenseFromRow/createExpense calls without full splits.
- `CI=true` turns on -Werror: match on enums/sealed traits must stay exhaustive, and unused imports fail the build. Run only targeted tests: `sbt "web/testOnly *XSpec"` / `sbt "server/testOnly *XSpec"`, or `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Never run the full suite. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH (the default shell node is v16, so yarn install fails). Server tests need Docker (testcontainers).
- CLAUDE.md rules: no hacks/timing workarounds; no silent defaults for missing data; match the surrounding style (doc comments on public logic functions, as in BankStatementReviewLogic); keep changes surgical.

## Non-obvious notes
- `rowInfo`'s `ruleList` is already the effective rules, but the forms receive the explicit rules and call `effectiveRules` themselves. Use the same verdict in both places so the table and the form agree.
- The Ignore check in `primaryActionFor` comes before ReviewRefund, so ignore-matched credits already get IgnoreByRule. Credits never get an expense match (`expenseMatches` is debit-only), so in `bulkRowDecision` the refund check must run before the "No category" fallback.
- An explicit SetMerchant rule can reference a merchant that isn't in the loaded list. Display code already resolves names through `merchants.find`, and form initialSelection drops unknown ids.
- `bulkImportSummary` has no refund bucket. Count created refunds under `created` unless you change the summary on purpose (update its spec if you do).

findings.title: fullSplit helper creates a duplicate "Test Category" when called twice for one user, breaking multi-expense tests

reason.text: False positive. The POST /categories endpoint goes through CreateCategoryAction, which calls CategoriesRepository.getOrCreate (createIfAbsent, then findByName), so a repeated name returns the existing category instead of hitting the unique constraint. The only translation to 'A category with that name already exists' is in update. The affected specs (Expenses, Documents, Receipts, Savings and others) ran under Docker with 171 passed and 0 failed.

findings.title: fullSplit helper creates the same category name each call, which collides on the per-user unique constraint

reason.text: False positive, same reason as I2.1. CreateCategoryAction uses getOrCreate, which is idempotent by name, and the listed specs passed in a real Docker run (171 passed, 0 failed).

reason.text: Out of scope. The task covered the paths that go through ExpenseValidator (the web and API forms). The Telegram bot and web-app flows let users log an expense without a category on purpose, so rejecting those messages would change how the bot behaves. That needs the user's decision and is not something to fold into this fix.
